summary:
G01 (TF-0289) implemented: every `AppErrorCode` now carries a stable, permission-scoped recovery entry and `AppError` instances expose `retryable` + `nextAction`.

Change set (verified byte-for-byte against the pristine `base/` checkout: exactly 1 modified + 5 added files):
- `src/lib/error-model.ts` — added `NEXT_ACTION_KINDS` (`retry|reauthenticate|reconfigure|open-settings|contact-support`), `RECOVERY_SCOPES` (`self-retry`/`user-action-required`), `ErrorRecovery`, `ERROR_RECOVERY_TABLE` (14 rows, one per class), `getErrorRecovery`/`getNextAction` (fail-closed to the `UNKNOWN` row). `AppError` now carries `recovery`/`retryable`/`nextAction` read from the same table, so an instance can never disagree with it; `normalizeAppError` reuses that constructor. Retryable is exactly the six self-retry classes (TIMEOUT, RATE_LIMIT, CHANNEL_UNAVAILABLE, NETWORK, GATEWAY, OVERLOADED) with action exactly `{ kind: 'retry' }` — same set as the existing `ERROR_COPY.retryable`; the other eight are `user-action-required` and never `retry`; `UNKNOWN` keeps `action: null` so the raw error is exposed rather than faked as repairable. Action keys are limited to `kind`(+`target`); no command/script/shell/exec/argv field exists anywhere in the surface. No second envelope, error class or code union was introduced.
- `tests/unit/error-recovery-next-action.test.ts` (6 tests), `harness/specs/tasks/harness-gap-error-recovery-next-action.md`, `docs/dev/harness-gap-closure/g01-error-recovery-next-action.md`, `docs/dev/harness-gap-closure/g01-acceptance.json`, `docs/dev/harness-gap-closure/G01-SHA256SUMS`.

Disclosures: (1) this isolated workspace had `tests/unit/error-governance-boundary.test.ts` stripped although the error-governance rule names it as a required pre-existing guard; I restored it byte-identically (sha256 a12da838c995f6f6626c83e179e15e4988d5328bf6071b597c471b89afdd6c08) so the governance check and the guard suite could actually run — it is unmodified. (2) No dependencies were installed and no network was used: I temporarily junctioned the machine's existing local pnpm store as `node_modules` to execute vitest/eslint/tsgo, then removed the junction and verified the external store is intact and no `node_modules`/`.git` remains in the workspace. (3) `harness run --dry-run` and `comms:replay/compare` are not executable in this checkout (no git metadata: `assertDiffBase` fails closed on `origin/main`, replay depends on `git log`); both fail before doing any work and neither touches the changed surface.

Residual: the repo-wide `typecheck:test`/`typecheck:web` banners carry only pre-existing errors (missing build-generated `_ext-bridge.generated`, 884 runtime implicit-any errors) with 0 diagnostics in touched files; one unrelated runtime test file cannot load because the shared store has no Windows-resolvable `tslog`.
